issues: [High/Cross-scene continuity & consistency] Timeline contradictions regarding the first/second coffees and what she learned 'today'. — Scene 6 explicitly jumps to the 2nd Saturday, which means Scene 7 (where she makes her 'second' coffee and improves her milk frothing) happens a week after her first coffee in Scene 4, awkwardly disrupting the continuous learning progression of her first shift. Furthermore, in Scene 9 (the 3rd Saturday), Maya says she learned to froth milk correctly 'today' ('i dag'), but that breakthrough already happened in Scene 7. Scene 9 should reflect what she learned over all her shifts so far, rather than just that day.

[Med/Naive whole-week listener (no checklist)] Unrealistic key-holding for a brand new volunteer — In Scene 2, Maya unlocks the café's front door alone on her very first day before the other volunteers arrive, and in Scene 9 she locks up the café alone. It breaks realism slightly that a day-1 volunteer would be given the keys to open and close the shop unsupervised.

[Med/Cross-scene continuity & consistency] Continuity gap in the 'learning to make coffee' arc between Scenes 4, 6, and 7. — In Scene 4 (first Saturday), Maya's first flawed coffee is a cappuccino. Scene 6 advances the timeline to her second Saturday. Scene 7 then continues the morning, but Maya makes a latte and says 'It was only my second latte today. The first cup was not quite perfect.' Changing the drink from cappuccino to latte and spanning the arc across a week gap makes it sound like she is referring to a new, off-screen mistake made that same morning, which loses the direct payoff of her improving from her first attempt in Scene 4.

[Low/Repetition & monotony] Verbatim line repetition from previous scene — Scene 2 repeats the exact sentence 'Jeg har aldrig arbejdet på en café før.' that was just used at the very end of Scene 1. While reinforcing grammar/vocabulary is good, repeating a full identical sentence verbatim across consecutive scenes can sound like a copy-paste error rather than natural pedagogical recurrence.

[Low/Cross-scene continuity & consistency] Maya unlocking the café alone on her very first day. — Maya unlocks the heavy front door and starts setting up before the other volunteers arrive on her very first shift. Logistically, it's slightly illogical that a brand-new volunteer would already have the keys to the shop before meeting anyone for her first shift.

[High/Naive whole-week listener (no checklist)] Maya opens the café alone on her very first day. — She goes into the back room, puts on an apron, and unlocks the heavy front door before any other volunteers arrive. It breaks immersion that a brand-new volunteer showing up for her first shift would already have a key and be opening the venue alone.

[Low/Repetition & monotony] Exact sentence repetition from the previous scene. — Scene 2 repeats the exact sentence 'Jeg har aldrig arbejdet på en café før' shortly after it was used as the concluding line of Scene 1. While vocabulary repetition is pedagogically useful, repeating a full 9-word sentence verbatim across adjacent scenes can feel slightly like a copy-paste error rather than natural reinforcement.

[Med/Cross-scene continuity & consistency] Muddled continuity of the 'first vs. second coffee' arc. — In Scene 4, Maya makes a cappuccino (her first coffee) but fails to get thick foam. In Scene 7, she makes a latte, calls it her 'second latte today', but then directly compares it to 'the first cup' not being perfect and celebrates getting 'thick foam' this time. This mixes up the drinks (thick foam is meant for cappuccinos) and makes the connection between her first and second coffee attempts confusing.

[Med/Naive whole-week listener (no checklist)] Mismatched drink reference for the milk-frothing payoff — In Scene 7, Maya makes a 'latte' and notes 'Den første kop var ikke helt perfekt', which emotionally pays off her struggle with milk foam in Scene 4. However, in Scene 4 she made a 'cappuccino', not a latte. Making them the same drink would make the callback much tighter for the learner.
